processing: An oven-dried green: leaf is spread, fixed at high heat, rolled, shaped into strands, dried in stages, graded and reheated to lift the aroma.
harvest_season: Spring is the finest, with picking starting around Qingming on one bud with one or two leaves.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, even strands in glossy dark green, with silvery down on the buds.
taste_profile: A mellow, fresh, smooth cup with mild astringency and a lingering sweetness.

brewing.notes: A glass works well. Water around 80–85°C keeps it sweet; large-leaf green turns harsh when it is scorched.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's tea, with spring lots graded by picking time and tenderness. Like other Yunnan greens, it is best within about a year. Check that the seller means the Dali tea, not a generic Yunnan green under a snowy name.
description:
Cangshan Xuelü, or Cangshan Snow Green, is a green tea from the foothills of the Cangshan range above Erhai Lake in Dali. It is a modern creation, not an old local tea.

It uses Mengku large-leaf plants, grown at about 2,000 metres. The processing is oven-dried, with staged drying, which gives fine dark strands with silver tips rather than the flat look of a pan-fired green.

Expect a smooth and mellow body and a sweet finish, with mild astringency if you keep the water cool enough. It is a soft cup for a large-leaf tea, and most people ruin that by using water that is too hot.

It sits in the wider Dian Lü family of Yunnan oven-dried greens, along with Nannuo Baihao. Buy spring lots and ask for the picking date. It is also a natural choice for trying the Bai three-course tea at home, a custom it is associated with in Dali.
history:
Cangshan Xuelü was developed at the Xiaguan Tea Factory in 1964. It was named a provincial famous tea of Yunnan three times between 1980 and 1983, and received a quality award from China's agriculture ministry in 1989.

Little else is documented about its early years. The variant name Cangshan Lüxue also appears in Chinese lists of famous teas.
